source_document.body:
Chinese fast-fashion giant Shein said on Wednesday that soft demand in its European business could take a year to recover from new e-commerce import fees and has also agreed to pay $100 million to settle U.S. Federal Trade Commission claims that it misled consumers about shipping times and products.
Shein Global Holdings ( HKSE: 0625 ) reported adjusted net income of $790 million for the third quarter ended Sept. 30, up 27% year over year, as net revenue declined 6% to $10.27 billion. Profit increased despite the revenue decline as the company cut costs.
Europe was the weakest region for the newly listed online retailer. The European Union in July implemented a 3 euro ($3.36) fee on low-value packages entering the bloc and on Nov. 1 imposed an additional 2 euro ($2.24) parcel handling charge. Revenue in Europe fell 27.6% to $2.98 billion in the quarter after Shein raised prices to offset the additional costs.
The fees apply to each different product category within a package, meaning that a shipment with four distinct items could be subject to customs fees of nearly $22.
The new rules eliminating duty-free status on so-called de minimis shipments are designed to slow entry of low-cost, subsidized and unethically sourced Chinese imports that undercut domestic manufacturers and retailers, and also provide a conduit for drug smuggling. The regulatory change significantly reduced the competitive advantage for China-based marketplaces and stores like Shein, forcing them to set up local fulfillment warehouses and ship goods in bulk through traditional ocean and air freight channels rather than directly to consumers from overseas.
Shein’s local fulfillment program in Europe, which it calls Flash Forward-Deployed Inventory, handles more than 40% of deliveries to European customers. The company expects that share to climb to about 50% by the end of the year. Products fulfilled through the program have higher conversion rates and generate more profit per item than those shipped cross-border, the company said.
CEO Sky Xu told analysts during an earnings briefing that European sales likely would not bounce back until the second half of 2027.
Lower revenue figures reflected the slump in Europe, but also a 9.4% decline in the United States, which last year hiked tariffs on small-dollar parcel imports.
Xu told analysts that the company is putting more resources into Latin America and other regions to reduce dependence on Europe and North America.
Alleged deceptive practices
The Federal Trade Commission on Tuesday announced that Shein will pay $100 million to address allegations that the company violated the law by making it difficult to resolve purchase issues, failed to keep its shipping promises, suppressed negative reviews and made deceptive supply chain claims, including about the origin of cotton products.
“Shein attracted consumers with promises of affordable clothing, fast delivery and use of suppliers that earned above-average ratings on standards related to child and forced labor, among other representations,” said Christopher Mufarrige, director of the FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection, in a statement. “In reality, the company misled millions of consumers about its products, its suppliers and the authenticity of its customer reviews. Shein further compounded consumer harm by making it extraordinarily difficult to obtain customer service.”
The FTC alleged in a complaint that Shein marketed fast, transparent and reliable shipping, but tens of thousands of consumers reported that their orders arrived days, weeks or months late, while some consumers never received their orders at all. Shein did not provide consumers with adequate shipping updates, including legally required delay notices, and consumers were unable to reach customer service to inquire about late or missing orders.
Shein ships nearly one million packages to the United States each day, but only employed five customer service agents as of September 2025 to handle telephone inquiries from American consumers and failed to provide a phone number for those agents on its website. Consumer requests often went unanswered, according to the FTC.
The FTC also alleged that Shein systematically prevented reviews from being displayed on its website in violation of the law, publishing positive reviews while suppressing or deleting reviews from customers who criticized or returned Shein’s products.
Shein also made unsupported claims regarding its evoluSHEIN products. Although the company marketed evoluSHEIN products as sourced from suppliers with above-average ratings in social-compliance audits designed to protect against child and forced labor, the FTC alleges that SHEIN failed to provide a single audit that supported those claims.
Shein’s representations about the country of origin for cotton used in its products are also deceptive, according to the complaint. Cotton that Shein represented as U.S.-grown, for example, was found to originate from China, and cotton used in at least some of its products could not be traced to any country of origin at all.
In addition to paying $100 million to resolve the complaint, Shein has agreed not to misrepresent shipping and delivery times, suppress negative product reviews, and make deceptive claims about supplier and manufacturer audits or product traceability, while also increasing its customer service workforce.
In a statement, the company said it had reached an agreement to resolve the investigation, which it said related to “certain historical business practices.” The company also said that it disagrees with the FTC’s characterisations, but was taking steps to bolster its compliance practices.
Towards that end, Shein is also hosting a series of compliance sessions with third-party experts to educate marketplace sellers on EU chemical safety regulations and compliance requirements for high-risk substances in consumer products, as well as for safety and compliance requirements for lithium batteries in consumer electronics. The sessions are designed to help small businesses better understand and comply with regulatory requirements for products sold into the EU.

Aerial view of a large-scale nickel mining site on a tropical island near Wayag, Raja Ampat, Indonesia. ( Image by Tom | AdobeStock. )
By: Northern Miner Staff November 25, 2026
A sulphur shortage threatens projects that would add more than 600,000 tonnes of nickel capacity in Indonesia ’s battery-materials sector, Wood Mackenzie said Wednesday.
Indonesia had relied on the Middle East for about 80% of its sulphur imports before the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Sulphur imports fell 29% year-over-year in the first half of 2026 and average prices nearly tripled, the consultancy reported .
“Sulphur supply constraints are unlikely to ease quickly,” Wood Mackenzie research associate Ziyi Liu said. “Logistics normalisation takes time even if conflict-related disruptions subside, and persistent competition from the fertiliser sector limits the reallocation of available supply to industrial buyers.”
Indonesian plants use sulphur to make the acid that extracts nickel and cobalt from ore for use in batteries. Their high-pressure acid leach process produces mixed hydroxide precipitate, an intermediate used to make battery chemicals.
Sulphur accounts for roughly half the operating cost of these plants, the International Energy Agency estimates. Indonesia, the world’s biggest nickel producer, mined an estimated 2.6 million tonnes in 2025, according to the United States Geological Survey . That represents about two-thirds of world output.
Production cuts
Drought has also hit operating plants. Smelters at the Indonesia Morowali Industrial Park on Sulawesi reported production cuts of 30% to 45% in late September as water grew scarce and barges struggled to deliver coal, Wood Mackenzie said.
The squeeze extends to stainless steel. Falling grades in Indonesian ore have cut production of nickel pig iron, a lower-grade nickel product, prompting stainless mills to buy more pure nickel and use more scrap.
Scrap now makes up about a quarter of the stainless-steel feed mix, up from 21% to 22% a few years ago, Wood Mackenzie estimates.
Even with mills buying more pure nickel, Wood Mackenzie expects a surplus of high-purity metal to persist unless supply also falls. It forecasts that global consumption of refined cobalt will decline this year. The London Metal Exchange cash nickel price settled at $15,060 (C$21,530) per tonne Tuesday.

The Waterfront Calls: Gallaxy 10 Houseboat Promises a Lifestyle You'll Never Want To Trade Back
27 photos
Photo: Galla Yachts
There are so many ways to approach the mobile lifestyle. We have teardrop trailers, campers, motorhomes, destination trailers, boats, yachts, and more. But somewhere along the lines, someone thought of combining the comforts of home with the abilities of a boat. Thus, the houseboat was born.
If the term houseboat is new to you, which, if you follow along with our content, it shouldn’t be, allow me to point out that these constructions aim to bring the luxuries of home into the aquatic domain. To achieve such a feat, houseboats are typically built upon a platform built with pontoons for flotation upon which a superstructure is added. It’s in this superstructure that we see the home side of things.
Photo: Galla Yachts What are the benefits of such a machine? Let’s think about that for a minute. First and foremost, houseboats serve as gorgeous and comfortable vacation homes ready to go once you’re set to take some days off your calendar. Sure, there are docking and upkeep fees to consider, but that’s a different story.
However, some people use these structures for year-round living, and if we consider that the option before us today, the Gallaxy 10, is priced at €132,500 ($145,500) without motorization and transaction fees, well, with the way the housing market is looking these days, a houseboat may just be the deal of the decade.
Now, we’ve seen houseboats before here on autoevolution, but it’s not everyday that one looks this good, envelopes its owners in a particular level of luxury that’s bound to feel like home, and unlocks a particular side of life that will have you wondering why you live in a landlocked home in the first place.
Photo: Galla Yachts I mean, if I woke up in a bedroom pointed at the horizon and the sun beating in, I’m already won over. Toss in a complete kitchen that I can use to fill the airwaves with the smell of freshly ground and brewed coffee in the morning, a terrace on which I can enjoy that coffee, and I’m starting to look for ways to start making some serious cash, enough for a down payment on one of these; the rest I’ll work out along the way.
If you throw in a roof-top terrace , such as what we see in the Gallaxy 10 and it’s 12 brethren, then by god, you’ll have me questioning my life’s choices, as I already am. I’m sorry if I’m coming across like this is one of the most beautiful lifestyle experiences you can have, because it sort of is, and is a lot more accessible than we think.
Think about things this way. The Gallaxy 10, with it’s price tag, is one of the more luxurious and roomy houseboat options on the market, and some out there cruise in for around a third less. So yes, even with port docking fees alone, which depend on the size of your boat, you’re still looking at an achievable dream. There are a ton of beautiful places out there; find one and explore its shores.
Photo: Galla Yachts As for the Gallaxy 10, there are a few things that make this houseboat stand apart from others on the market, and aside from two layouts, suitable for up to six people, I couldn’t believe that Galla Yachts, the minds and hands behind the design, still manage to give owners access to features like a hot-stone sauna. It’s not a common feature in a houseboat.
Interior appliances and furnishings also bring forth a balanced feeling to the home and give off that Scandinavian or IKEA-like feel. I’m sure you can talk things over with the folks at Galla to make changes to the furniture.
What I also found rather nice about this design is that Galla has thought it up to be one that taps into solar energy. Be it for the propulsion or the appliances inside, we don’t know for sure, but usually both can be operated on electricity alone, helping reduce fees and costs that you’re exposed to throughout the year.
Photo: Galla Yachts As I explored the Gallaxy 10 , I did notice some images that showcase the boat being pushed around by an outboard motor, and electric options do exist on the market these days; weight your costs and long-term savings and go from there.
What I couldn’t make out from the spec sheet, mainly because it’s in German, is how large of a battery array we can tap into. But, being, in essence, a home, you can always bring along a battery bank or two, some portable solar panels, and go from there. Maybe just plug the bank into a wall socket and recharge that way.
I’m not saying that the house-boating lifestyle is the perfect way to do off-grid and mobile living, but it is an option that I highly recommend. I’ve spent some days on pontoons myself, and it’s a bit of a different kind of experience, one I yearn for year after year; the waterfront calls.

Amazon Autos UK Going Live in 2027, but Dealers Still Get the Last Word
7 photos
Photo: Amazon
As you're well aware, Amazon is a completely different animal from the company's virtual bookstore and distributor-back retail model from the 1990s. The Washington-based colossus has become very good at removing people from the buying process, be it groceries, car parts, or actual cars. Buying a vehicle through Amazon Autos in Britain, however, will still require a trip to the dealer.
The company founded by Jeff Bezos in Bellevue more than three decades ago is bringing its online car marketplace to the United Kingdom in 2027, yet a few steps remain firmly in dealer territory. Paperwork, final sale, and handover, for example, will be handled by dealers throughout the United Kingdom.
Amazon Autos UK's debut sounds less revolutionary than the marketing suggests, but nevertheless, Amazon Autos could become a disruptor in this part of the world. The American corporation wants to control the part of the transaction that matters the most for many customers, specifically when the customer starts searching with the purpose of deciding which model is worth their hard-earned money.
South Korean automaker Hyundai is the first confirmed brand. Amazon's partner will kick things off in the United Kingdom with a selection of electric and internal combustion vehicles, including the new Ioniq 3 , the larger Ioniq 5, the Kona, and the i20. Used vehicles wearing the Hyundai badge will also be featured, while Vertu Motors will supply additional used vehicle listings.
More automakers and retailers will be announced before the platform goes live in the first part of 2027. The shopping process will be pretty familiar to anyone who has bought something from Amazon. For starters, customers have search tools that allow them to search by model, trim, and paint color. They can also view upfront prices, available stock, and obtain an indicative valuation of their old car.
Photo: Amazon Naturally, the platform allows them to investigate personal contract purchase and hire purchase finance options. After reserving the vehicle of their liking, the customer has to contact the chosen dealer to complete the purchase in person. Retailers are the ones who set the final price and retain the customer relationship, and Amazon cannot do anything about it, even though it would like to.
Think of Amazon Autos UK as the showroom before the showroom, if that makes sense. Amazon wants prospective customers to do their research using its tools, narrow down their choices, and hit the dealer knowing which car they intend to purchase. Considering that online inquiries sometimes involve buyers who are still months away from buying anything, that could be useful for retailers.
Customers who already made their minds in regard to what car and finance option they want is a valuable lead. More valuable than someone asking over the phone whether a particular model comes in blue. This arrangement, however, also reveals the limits of Amazon's ambitions in the UK's online car market, which is led by Autotrader.
Britain's established online automotive marketplace has a ginormous advantage in inventory and dealer relations. Autotrader's latest half-year report shows around 13,900 retailer forecourts advertising on the platform, but nevertheless, Amazon is the much bigger corporation that would surely win a war of attrition.
From the looks of it, Amazon's initial focus in the UK is less about persuading car buyers to use its platform in lieu of Autotrader. Instead, the American newcomer is likely using its strengths to convince dealers to view its platform as a viable option.

Hyundai’s new IONIQ 3 checks all the boxes as an affordable EV: it offers over 300 miles of range, a practical interior, and Hyundai’s new Pleos infotainment system. So, will Hyundai bring it to the US?
Is Hyundai launching the IONIQ 3 in the US?
The Hyundai IONIQ 3 is now on sale across Europe and the UK as a smaller sibling to the IONIQ 5, positioned between the Inster EV and Hyundai Kona Electric.
Although it’s part of the IONIQ sub-brand, the IONIQ 3 features a new “Aero Hatch” design. The new look “reimagines the compact EV silhouette,” Hyundai said, designed to optimize efficiency and interior space.
The response so far has been “extraordinary,” Ashley Andrew, president of Hyundai Motor UK, said after launching the IONIQ 3 last month.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
According to Andrew, the compact EV received “more customers registering their interest before launch than any new Hyundai we’ve introduced in the UK,” and that’s including gas-powered and electric vehicles.
The first reviews of the IONIQ 3 have been overwhelmingly positive, highlighting its efficiency, practical interior, and affordable price tag.
Update 11/25/2026: A Hyundai spokesperson told Electrek that “it’s likely that the IONIQ 3 that was apparently spotted in the US recently was the same unit that was brought in for World Car of the Year’s annual test days” held in Pasadena, California.
It looks like the IONIQ 3 will be another affordable, practical EV the US will miss out on.
View this post on Instagram A post shared by KindelAuto (@kindelauto)
The update from Hyundai comes after the IONIQ 3 was recently captured driving on public US roads, raising speculation, or perhaps hope, that it will come to the States after all.
The model spotted in the images from KindelAuto is the IONIQ 3 N Line, a sportier, higher-priced trim.
While it’s among the first sightings in the US, we have seen several Hyundai Motor Group electric vehicles testing in the US that are still not available and likely won’t ever be, such as Kia’s EV5 SUV and PV5 van.
Hyundai IONIQ 3 N-Line (Source: Hyundai UK)
The IONIQ 3 is built at Hyundai Motor’s Izmit, Turkey, plant and is specifically designed for European drivers.
In Europe and the UK, Hyundai offers the IONIQ 3 with two battery packs: 42 kWh and 61 kWh. The base IONIQ 3 Advance trim with the 42 kWh battery starts at £18,495 ($25,000) OTR and offers up to 213 miles of WLTP range. That’s including the UK’s £3,750 Electric Car Grant.
Hyundai IONIQ 3 interior (Source: Hyundai)
The IONIQ 3 Advance with the 61 kWh battery starts at £21,995 ($29,000) and offers a “class-leading” WLTP range of up to 308 miles. That also includes the UK government ECG grant.
Measuring 4,155 mm (163.5″) long, 1,800 mm (70.9″) wide, and 1,505 mm (59.3″) high, with a wheelbase of 2,680 mm (105.5″), Hyundai’s electric hatch is even smaller than the Kia EV3 and Volkswagen ID.3.
The IONIQ 3 is also Hyundai’s first vehicle in Europe equipped with its new Pleos Connect infotainment system.
Hyundai IONIQ 3 interior with Pleos Connect infotainment system (Source: Hyundai)
Hyundai’s new system is more like using a smartphone. It’s based on the Android Automotive OS with apps and customizable screens, similar to Tesla models. It’s available in the IONIQ 3 with a 12.9″ or 14.6″ center infotainment screen, plus an optional driver display.
Unlike the larger IONIQ 5, the IONIQ 3 uses a 400V architecture. However, the 42 kWh battery can still recharge from 10% to 80% in about 29 minutes. The 61 kWh battery takes around 30 minutes.
In Germany and other European markets, Hyundai’s compact IONIQ 3 starts at about €28,950 ($33,000).
Hyundai IONIQ 3 (Source: Hyundai UK)
While Hyundai currently has no plans to bring the IONIQ 3 to the US, it does sell the IONIQ 5, built at the Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America outside Savannah, GA, alongside the three-row IONIQ 9.
Starting at about $35,000, Hyundai’s IONIQ 5 has remained among the top-selling electric vehicles in the US outside of the Tesla Model Y and Model 3.
In fact, Hyundai was just named the “Best Electric Vehicle Brand” by US News & World Report for the first time for 2027.

Rapper 2 Chainz Wrecks Bright Orange Cybertruck in Head-On Collision
9 photos
Photo: Instagram/2 Chainz (Composite)
If how you start your Monday is any indication of how the rest of the week will be like, rapper 2 Chainz has had much better weeks than this one. He was involved in a head-on, two-vehicle accident on Monday, resulting in broken ribs and two totaled cars.
On Tuesday (November 24), rapper 2 Chainz took to social media with a message for his fans, his supporters, and friends, many of whom had probably been trying to get a hold of him. That message was a confirmation that he'd been involved in a highway crash the night before and an assurance that he was ok.
Not the same could be said about his custom Tesla Cybertruck , the other vehicle involved in the accident, and probably the other driver as well. 2 Chainz, whose real name is Tauheed Epps, only offered details pertaining to his involvement, while making sure that he clarified that he wasn't the one to have caused the accident.
The other driver did.
Photo: Instagram | 2chainz In a caption to the video, which you can also see in the embed below, the rapper wrote that he suffered broken ribs but was otherwise fine – resting, as per the doctor's orders. He also made sure he set the record straight before any false rumors got out, saying, "no I wasn't drinking, smoking, sleeping or on auto pilot, the other driver dodged a possum and hit me head on."
The video shows a silver car in the middle of the road, with first responder vehicles in the background. It then spins to one side where, at some distance in a ditch, is the rapper's bright orange Cybertruck . The woman shooting the video says something as she starts shooting, but it's probably in reference to something else because she's asking another person to "hold on."
Both vehicles involved are probably totaled, and there's no information on the condition of the other driver. In a later IG Story, 2 Chainz reconnected to his fans, showing them the large amount of pills he'd been prescribed and casually wondering out loud about how freely doctors hand out addictive drugs.
Photo: Instagram | 2chainz This is actually the second serious car accident for the rapper in just three years, as he was previously hospitalized in December 2023 after another car slammed into his.
2 Chainz was in the later wave of celebrities jumping on the Cybertruck bandwagon, getting his sometime in 2024 and setting out to customize it right away. In June of that same year, he was showing it off on his social media, tagging Roadshow International for the custom orange wrap with wolf decals on either side and Forgiato for the alloy wheels.
Photo: Instagram/2 Chainz They say that beauty is in the eye of the beholder, and it definitely proved true when 2 Chainz publicly revealed his orange truck – a wild spin on a vehicle that was already very controversial. That's probably why he ended up deleting that post.
Whatever the reason was, if he was having any sort of buyer's remorse, he's past that now. View this post on Instagram A post shared by 2 Chainz Aka Tity Boi (@2chainz)

Drill cores at Jaguar Uranium's Berlin project in Colombia. Credit: Jaguar Uranium
Posted By: Blair McBride November 25, 2026
An initial resource from Jaguar Uranium (NYSE-A: JAGU) for its Berlin critical metals project in Colombia outlines 40% more inferred tonnes but about half the uranium grade and 29% fewer contained pounds than a historical estimate by the previous owner.
Berlin holds 937,000 indicated tonnes grading 561 parts per million (ppm) uranium oxide (U 3 O 8 ) for 1.2 million lb. U 3 O 8 and 11.3 million inferred tonnes at 562 ppm U 3 O 8 for 14.1 million lb. U 3 O 8 , Jaguar reported Wednesday . SLR International prepared the resource, effective Nov. 5.
Berlin held 600,000 indicated tonnes grading 0.11% U 3 O 8 for 1.5 million lb. and 8.1 million inferred tonnes at 0.11% U 3 O 8 , or 1,100 ppm, for 19.9 million lb., as reported by former owner U3O8 Corp. in 2012 . The earlier estimate used a uranium-grade cutoff of 0.04%, while Jaguar’s uses $245 (C$350) per tonne as its net smelter return cutoff, incorporating the value of other metals, and limits the resource to material considered potentially mineable underground.
“We have defined a uranium resource alongside a suite of critical mineral and strategic metal co-products, including rare earth oxides, vanadium, nickel, zinc, molybdenum and phosphate,” Jaguar CEO Steven Gold said in a release, noting that the metals occur across 2.9 km of a 10.5-km trend that’s open to the north.
“With a strong balance sheet and no debt, we are well-funded to advance further exploration activity.”
Jaguar shares rose 4.7% to 63.4¢ apiece by 10:18 a.m. Wednesday in New York, for a market capitalization of $12.8 million.
Critical metals spread
Berlin’s other metals could be important to its economic prospects. Jaguar says material grading 400 to 600 ppm U 3 O 8 can qualify for the resource because the potential value of vanadium, phosphate, rare earths and other metals lifts it above the $245-per-tonne net smelter return cutoff.
Berlin is about 150 km northwest of Bogotá in Caldas department.
The 937,000 indicated tonnes also grade 50,474 ppm phosphorus pentoxide (P₂O₅) for about 47,300 contained tonnes. Other grades include 3,170 ppm vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅) for 2,970 tonnes, zinc at 1,830 ppm for 1,715 tonnes and nickel at 1,094 ppm for 1,025 tonnes.
Jaguar plans additional drilling, including infill to upgrade inferred resources to indicated, though it hasn’t specified targets in metres.
The company acquired Berlin in 2024 from Green Shift Commodities (TSXV: GCOM), formerly U3O8 Corp., in a cash-and-shares deal that included C$20,000, 1.21 million Jaguar shares and a 1% net smelter return royalty at closing. Jaguar paid another C$1 million and issued shares valued at $15.3 million when it listed in February.

Australia’s Lynas is the only major producer of separated rare earths outside China. ( Image courtesy of Lynas Rare Earths. )
Posted By: Northern Miner Staff November 25, 2026
Western buyers are paying steep premiums for rare earths as China restricts exports. Whether those premiums can help finance new mines and refineries outside China depends on the price buyers will guarantee for years, Sprott (TSX, NYSE: SII) says.
High-purity yttrium oxide, used in jet engine coatings, traded at about $1,650 (C$2,360) per kg in North America on Nov. 17, roughly 185 times the Chinese price of about $9. Few processors outside China can supply the separated rare earths manufacturers need, Sprott’s Paul Wong and Jacob White wrote in a Nov. 24 report on the sector.
“Higher prices cannot quickly resolve this concentration,” Wong and White wrote. “Secure supply requires separation, refining, metallurgy and magnet manufacturing, not simply new mines.”
The price a buyer pays for scarce oxide today tells a lender little about what a refinery will earn once it opens. A long-term contract with a minimum price gives the lender a figure it can use to judge whether the project can repay a construction loan. The yttrium price gap is likely to narrow, but even a smaller premium could make Western projects viable, the authors said.
In California, MP Materials (NYSE: MP) has a 10-year agreement with the U.S. Department of Defense that sets a $110-per-kg floor for neodymium-praseodymium in products it sells or stockpiles from its Mountain Pass mine. MP booked $8.1 million in price protection income in the quarter to Sept. 30, the company said this month.
Australia’s Lynas Rare Earths (ASX: LYC; US-OTC: LYSCF) had minimum prices in place for more than half its output by late October. Offering dysprosium and terbium alongside neodymium and praseodymium helps Lynas win longer contracts with magnet makers, Interim CEO Pol Le Roux told analysts in October. Lynas set up a price floor for rare earth sales in March with JARE, a venture involving Japan’s Jogmec and Sojitz. In May 2025, Lynas became the first producer of separated heavy rare earth oxides outside China.
Export curbs
China mined 60% of the world’s magnet rare earths in 2024, refined 91% and made 94% of its sintered permanent magnets, according to the International Energy Agency . Dysprosium and terbium help those magnets retain their strength at the high temperatures inside electric motors.
In Europe, dysprosium oxide fetched about $4,875 per kg on Nov. 17, nearly 22 times the Chinese price. Terbium oxide traded at about $10,500 per kg in Europe against $944 in China, according to Benchmark Mineral Intelligence and Bloomberg figuref75s cited by Sprott.
China shipped an average of 19.3 tonnes a month of controlled rare earth compounds and metals to the U.S. from November 2025 through September, down 75% from 76.8 tonnes a month between June 2024 and March 2025, according to Sprott. It used trade figures from Silverado Policy Accelerator for products fully covered by China’s April 2025 export controls. The figures exclude finished magnets.
Beijing has suspended broader controls on rare earths and related technology through Jan. 10, 2027. The April licensing rules still apply to certain rare earths and magnets.
South Africa’s Steenkampskraal mine has lined up buyers in China for its first concentrate sales, expected in early 2027, Finance Chief Tyrone Searle told The Northern Miner in October. The operation is owned by privately held Steenkampskraal Monazite Mine.
The mine operator and France’s Remedy Metals have since signed a non-binding agreement to test whether they can separate rare earths at Steenkampskraal. They plan to start with ore samples in a laboratory before deciding whether to run a pilot at the mine, Mining Weekly reported Wednesday.
Equity financing
Developers raising money by selling shares face a tougher market. The Sprott Rare Earths Ex-China ETF (Nasdaq: REXC), which tracks rare earth companies outside China, closed at $11.09 Tuesday, down 30% from $15.76 on Sept. 30. A developer whose own shares fall must issue more of them to raise the same construction dollars.
Wong and White attributed much of the sell-off to investors cutting positions bought with borrowed money as markets grew more volatile. Net inflows into Sprott’s fund topped $100 million between April and Nov. 17, according to Bloomberg data compiled by the asset manager.

Operations at Ontario's Island Gold mine. Credit: Alamos Gold.
By: Northern Miner Staff November 25, 2026
A proposed Canadian tax break could leave new gold mines with about 30% more free cash flow in their first years of production, according to a BMO Capital Markets model. Larger miners with existing Canadian operations could see a more modest gain of about 3% in first-year operating cash flow, tapering after that, BMO’s mining analysts said late Tuesday in a report. Alamos Gold (TSX, NYSE: AGI) and Wesdome Gold Mines (TSX: WDO; US-OTC: WDOFF) are among the producers they expect to benefit most. Getting the deductions sooner “could help some marginal projects or brownfield expansions meet companies’ investment thresholds,” the Mining Association of Canada said on Sept. 15 when Ottawa announced the proposal. Ottawa’s proposed Productivity Mega Deduction would allow miners to deduct the full cost of qualifying Canadian development expenses incurred on or after Sept. 15, against taxable income in the year the expense was incurred. Eligible equipment acquired from that date could also be fully written off once it is available for use, the Finance Department said. Many capital deductions are currently spread over several years. The proposal would make immediate expensing permanent. It accelerates tax deductions rather than reimbursing companies for their spending.
Valuable overlap
For an established producer, deductions still owing on earlier investments would overlap with the full writeoff on new spending. That overlap is most valuable in the first year and fades as the old deductions are exhausted. A company already using accumulated losses to shelter its income would see less immediate benefit, BMO said. Tax remittance schedules would also affect when cash savings appear. Alamos spent $131.7 million (US$92.1 million) in growth capital at its Island Gold district in Ontario in the third quarter of 2026, much of it on the shaft, underground development and the Magino mill expansion. Alamos expects to commission the shaft in mid-2027, about one quarter later than previously planned, and finish expanding the mill in the first quarter of 2028, the company said in October . The tax proposal’s Sept. 15 eligibility date falls partway through that reporting period. The tax change would add about 7% to the net asset value of BMO’s model gold project, compared with about 2% for larger producers with Canadian operations, the bank said. The hypothetical developer’s internal rate of return would rise to 21% from 20%. BMO’s estimates assume provinces will follow Ottawa’s lead.
“This may seem minor, but the uplift in the near-term cash flow is meaningful,” the BMO analysts wrote.
M&A boost
Explorers and developers poised to benefit from larger tax deductions once their projects enter production include Snowline Gold (TSX: SGD; US-OTC: SNWGF), Troilus Mining (TSX: TLG; US-OTC: CHXMF) and Osisko Metals (TSX: OM; US-OTC: OMZNF), BMO said. However, limited taxable income early in a mine’s life could delay the cash savings for these companies, the bank said. Ottawa’s proposed mega-deduction could also encourage acquisitions by fully taxable producers, which could use eligible deductions from project spending to offset income from existing Canadian operations while adding future production, BMO said. Federal legislation is still pending. Ottawa reaffirmed its intention to proceed with the measure in the government’s most recent budget , which finance minister François-Philippe Champagne introduced Nov. 5.

Deliciously Retro and Fully Modern: The 2027 Vintage Cruiser 19RBS Travel Trailer Aims to Please
9 photos
Photo: YouTube/The RV Hunter
"The most stylish Work From Camper travel trailer on the road." That's how U.S.-based RV specialist Gulf Stream Coach Inch. describes the latest iteration of one of their most popular floorplans, the Vintage Cruiser 19RBS. It sounds great, but it still falls short of capturing everything that's great about it.
We could expand this description to include "retro," "modern," "quality build" and "versatile," but then, we'd be doing the job for the trailer. The brief first video at the bottom of the page can also serve this purpose, while the second is perfect for a more in-depth look.
Gulf Stream Coach has been working this "retro but modern" angle on their travel trailers for some years now. You can get their trailers as standard towables, or you can add optional Vintage Package for the full package, with matching exterior and interior, retro moon hub caps, and style cues that bring back the gorgeous '50s.
The one thing about these trailers that is not retro is the comfort they provide. The pull of nostalgia might feel irresistible to many, but I doubt all of these people would want the comfort you'd have in those days. So, Gulf Stream Coach loads up modern appliances inside this retro package and then works to make them integrate more or less organically.
Photo: YouTube/The RV Hunter The 19RBS we're looking at today has been around for 10 years, give or take a few months. It's an mid-level entry in the series of Lightweight Travel Trailers and was originally designed as a family-friendly unit .
It can still be that for 2027, but the spin is that it can also… not be. A traveling couple, for instance, would very much prefer a bar slash workspace counter facing the campsite window or, alternatively, a jackknife sofa for a lounge and the occasional guest. The old equipment, with a compact booth dinette, is still available.
The coffee bar slash desk option turns the 19RBS into a WFC (Work From Camper) trailer, Gulf Stream Coach says. It's a nice touch in an age where people are looking for ways to work even on vacation, no matter where they are.
Photo: YouTube/The RV Hunter Sizes, construction, and features of the 19RBS remain unchanged from previous years. This is a single-axle travel trailer measuring 23 feet 1 inch (7.03 meters) in total length built on a light six-sided aluminum frame. The shell is vacuum-bonded fiberglass with Azdel and a one-piece fiberglass roof, so you have the promise of a durable, minimal maintenance construction.
The unit that introduces the upgraded floorplan (and shown in both videos below) comes in Crimson red with a matching interior and knotty pine cabinetry. Nice touches outside include red piping on the sides of the trailer, new-for-2027 window eyebrows, and a rock guard painted to match.
Even the power tongue jack fits in the color scheme , and you will obviously get the same matchy-matchy treatment whether you choose teal or yellow for the exterior.
Photo: YouTube/The RV Hunter The layout is a front bedroom one, with the bathroom at the back, spread across the entire width of the trailer. The middle part of the trailer is taken up by the galley kitchen and the dinette, the bar/desk, or the jackknife sofa across from it.
This being a couple's coach, there is little concern for privacy, though Gulf Stream Coach does add a curtain to the bedroom space, so you can at least pretend you're getting some. Privacy, that is. Also here is a nice walkaround double bed with overhead cabinets, matching wardrobes, and reading lights.
The galley comes standard with a three-burner cooktop, a large stainless steel sink with a high-rise faucet, a small oven, an extractor, a microwave, and a decent 12V fridge. You get plenty of storage, both under the counter and above it, as well as a large pantry with a large counter on top that will work just fine as a kitchen extension.
Photo: YouTube/The RV Hunter Depending on whether you choose the old dinette or one of the two new options, storage will vary. The bar/desk arrangement seems to offer the highest number of compartments, so in addition to getting some work done or enjoying your meals with a view, you also get the possibility to pack heavier.
The bathroom is a standard three-piece one, dry and with nice finishes, including a porcelain toilet and a corner shower. It offers even more storage options in addition to the vanity and medicine cabinet, in the form of a linen closet and a full dresser with hanging space.
Standard features on the Vintage Cruiser 19RBS include a Fogatti on-demand tankless water heater, a 25,000-BTU furnace, a 15,000-BTU rooftop AC, a power awning, two marine-grade speakers outside, and prep for a backup camera. The cabinetry is real hardwood as standard, while the floor, walls, and ceiling are vinyl for easy care.
Photo: YouTube/The RV Hunter Also standard in the Vintage Package are the moon hub caps, the exterior graphics, Goodyear tires, and 100W of solar on the roof.
The 19RBS can hold 30 gallons (113 liters) of freshwater and 33 gallons (125 liters) of gray and black water, respectively. Dry weight is 3,119 lbs (1,414 kg), with 390 lbs (177 kg) of hitch weight and 1,261 lbs (572 kg) of cargo carrying capacity.
Sale prices for the 2027 model year will vary depending on your options and the dealer you get the unit from, but usually range between $24,000 and $30,000. As always, make sure you do your research before committing.

Tourne Cruise Edition Is a European All-Rounder Camper Van Built for All-Season Travel
24 photos
Photo: Tourne Campervans
The most appreciated camper vans for remote travel are those that combine everyday drivability with practicality, smart comfort, and self-sufficiency, and the Tourne Cruise Edition seems to check all of these boxes.
Built in Europe by Tourne Campervans, a small manufacturer based in Pivka, Slovenia, that specializes in hand-assembled, all-season-ready van conversions, the Tourne Cruise Edition is a four-berth camper that is fitted out for maximum comfort on the road. It combines a carefully planned interior with practical equipment aimed at making everyday touring comfortable, guaranteeing memorable travel experiences.
The Cruise Edition is one of the three models offered by Tourne Campervans, alongside the Tourne Expre and the Tourne Select. While the Tourne Expre is the entry-level option that offers an accessible starting point for all-season travel, the Tourne Select is the flagship model, featuring higher-end cabinetry and finishes, improved off-grid capabilities, and a more comprehensive cab technology package.
The Tourne Cruise is the mid-tier all-rounder and is the most popular model in the company’s lineup. It is offered as a pre-equipped camper van, with features that the team chose based on what their clients used the most in the past. As such, it provides all the essentials for convenient travels, while still leaving room for some optional extras.
Photo: Tourne Campervans Based on a Fiat Ducato chassis, the Cruise Edition camper van is available in two lengths. There is a 6-meter (19.7-foot) version and a 6.4-meter (21-foot) one, with the latter offering some extra living space and storage. The base vehicle uses a 2.2-liter Euro 6.4 diesel engine delivering 140 hp or 180 hp, paired with manual or automatic transmissions, depending on the chosen configuration.
For the exterior finish, white is the standard color, but clients can choose between several other options, including different shades of gray, black, blue and green. Designed to remain stealthy, the exterior is rather unadorned, with just the extra windows, a Thule awning, and the solar panel on the roof pointing at its camper identity.
The Cruise Edition comes with a painted front bumper, black skid plates, and full LED headlights, which is quite important when traveling at night. A Dometic Raintec RT100 outdoor light with rain cover and remote control is also installed on the passenger side, and an entry step makes getting in and out easier. The van rides on 16" alloy aluminum diamond black wheels and also comes equipped with a Monoblock towing hitch at the rear, an outdoor shower, and an external gas connection.
For the van’s interior, Tourne’s design approach focuses on Scandinavian-inspired simplicity, durability and practical use of space . The color scheme includes neutral tones, and all the furniture and cabinetry is made in the company’s own CNC facility using moisture-proof and scratch-resistant poplar panels and high-quality laminate protective surface layer. The end furniture strips are made of solid wood, and the furniture pieces are fitted with high-quality hardware.
Photo: Tourne Campervans An important thing that needs to be mentioned is that the company developed its camper van models in collaboration with Nordic partners, so they are built with year-round travel in mind. Features like high-performance elastomeric foam insulation, custom-fitted to the vehicle’s shape, diesel-powered heating, and integrated floor air channels designed to distribute warmth around the living area ensure you can travel comfortably in the Cruise in any season. An electric underfloor heating system can also be used when the van is connected to shore power.
In terms of layout, the Cruise Edition boasts an open-cab interior, with swiveling cab seats that become part of an extended seating area at the front. The swivel captain’s chairs pair with a two-passenger seatbelted bench and an adjustable table to create a nice dinette for four. A fifth person can join in, as there is also a small bench that slides out from inside the kitchen block.
The center of the van is occupied by a compact yet functional kitchen and an enclosed interior bathroom, while the rear of the van is dedicated to the main sleeping area. Instead of a fixed bed, the company opted for a modular Murphy-style bed, with removable cushions and a fold-away platform that opens up the garage area if you need more space for carrying bulky equipment.
Photo: Tourne Campervans One of the cleverest features inside the van is Tourne’s DREAM4 System, which allows the model to sleep up to four people without resorting to an elevator bed or a pop-top roof. This is a unique patented modular system that lets you transform the front dinette into another double bed measuring 185 by 120 cm (73 by 47 inches).
Though compact, the kitchen has more than enough storage and comes equipped with a two-burner gas hob, a sink, and a 90-liter refrigerator with a small freezer compartment. There is very little countertop for meal prep, but a flip-up extension and the front dining table come in handy in this regard.
Adding another layer of convenience , the indoor wet bathroom offers a shower, a small sink, a swivel toilet, and a wall-mounted cabinet for toiletries. It looks very sleek and modern, and is fully enclosed. Since we’re talking about the shower, it’s worth mentioning that the van’s water system includes a 95-liter (25-gallon) fresh water tank and a 100-liter (26-gallon) waste water tank.
There is also a roof vent in the bathroom, helping with ventilation after showering, and hangers and a rod lets you dry your clothes in here as well.

Porsche's Latest Aero Trickery Includes an Active Rudder System and an Active Split Rear Wing
27 photos
Photo: Porsche
Volkswagen Group brand Porsche has spent many decades teaching air to push its racing and production cars harder into the road, all in the name of lap times. The suits in Zuffenhausen and the mad lads in Weissach now intend to teach said air to push cars sideways, and the patent applications recently published by the Deutsches Patent- und Markenamt are as crazy as they get.
Simply put, both aerodynamic solutions proposed by Porsche could make racing and production cars change direction using forces normally left to the tires. One patent borrows vertical rudders from aircraft and boats, while the other divides the rear wing into two independently controlled sections. The latter solution effectively turns the rear wing into a tool for controlling yaw.
Both ideas may sound unhinged, but Weissach always had a nut loose in this regard. Modern performance vehicles generate a lot of downforce by default, but there are limits to how much additional cornering performance can be extracted by pressing the tires harder into the asphalt. Given the aforementioned, clever aero could do something other than push a given vehicle downward at speed.
DE102025117584A1 is the more unusual proposal, showing movable vertical fins positioned on the front hood and where the rear window is supposed to be on the 911. Indeed, the patent shows a big-winged 911 with two vents in the hood, which makes us believe that Porsche used the GT3 RS in this drawing.
The front and rear vertical fins act like rudders. Both rotate into the airflow, generating a sideways aerodynamic force. Redirecting flow to the sides produces a force that helps with changing the vehicle's direction, a principle that sounds very similar to how a boat's rudder works. The working fluid here is air, and the 911 GT3 RS is traveling considerably faster than a dinghy.
Photo: Porsche The patent's text notes two main rudders and at least one additional rudder. Positioning aerodynamic surfaces near both axles further gives the control system a way to influence the balance between the front and rear of the vehicle. The front rudder could influence the initial directional response, while the rear element could help manage stability once the car is loaded into a corner.
Per the patent, said aerodynamic trickery could also influence body roll, providing stability beyond the capabilities of a conventional suspension system. These rudders create drag, though. Catching an unexpected crosswind on a straight wouldn't help either, and a gust striking a large vertical fin while cornering at speed also sounds like a problem. And yes, visibility would be hindered as well.
Patent DE102025119020A1 was co-filed by Porsche and Volkswagen, detailing a rear wing that comprises two halves. When stowed, both sections are hidden flush into the rear deck. When activated, they swing outwards, leaving a central gap. A separate panel rises underneath to cover the opening left in the deck.
The mechanism is far more complicated than two little spoilers popping out of the trunk. Each half uses a parallelogram linkage, with four connecting arms tasked with controlling its movement. Telescoping rear links adjust the angle of attack, and the real trick here is that the halves don't have to operate symmetrically.
Porsche proposes giving the inner section a steeper angle when cornering, thus creating a difference in aerodynamic drag across the rear of the vehicle. This produces a yaw moment, helping rotate the car better. Porsche calls it aerodynamic torque vectoring, and the automaker further describes using the sections as an air brake by setting both halves at a steep angle.

Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-Front Angled 2
The Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H is an interesting little fanless appliance that pairs Intel’s new Panther Lake Core Ultra X7 368H processor with a dense industrial I/O layout. It packs a heterogeneous 16-core CPU, replaceable SODIMM memory and M.2 storage into a finned chassis that Supermicro rates for fanless operation in edge deployments.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H Key Specs (As Reviewed)
Processor | Intel Core Ultra X7 368H, 4P + 8E + 4 LPE (5.0GHz)
Operating System | Ubuntu Linux 26.04 LTS
Memory | 32GB DDR5-5600 (2x16GB SODIMM)
Storage | 256GB SSD (M.2 2280/2242, PCIe Gen5 x4) 1x M.2 2280 PCIe Gen4 x2 (Empty)
GPU | Intel Arc B390 (Xe3, 12 Xe cores)
PSU | 150W External Adapter
Form Factor | SFF Industrial PC
Dimensions | 185 x 83 x 140 mm (7.28 x 3.27 x 5.5in)
Weight | 1.47kg (3.25 lbs)
Networking | 2x 2.5GbE (Intel I226-IT) 1x 1GbE (Intel I219-LM)
Wireless | Empty (M.2 2230 E-Key Slot Available)
Color | Black
Ports | Front: 2x 10Gbps USB-A, 4x 480Mbps USB-A, 2x HDMI 2.1 , 2x 2.5GbE (RJ45), 1x 1GbE (RJ45), 2x COM (RS232), 1x GPIO (DB9)
Let us get to it.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H External Overview
Here is the front panel of the E103-14P-H, showing a dense array of industrial I/O. You can see three RJ45 Ethernet jacks labeled LAN1 through LAN3, alongside four white USB 2.0 Type-A ports and two red USB 3.2 Gen2 connectors.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-Front Angled 1
The front panel of the E103-14P-H carries most of the connectivity. This industrial gateway-style layout puts nearly everything you need to cable on one face. The chassis itself measures 185 x 83 x 140mm (7.28″ x 3.27″ x 5.5″) per Supermicro’s datasheet , which makes it a compact box that can sit on a DIN rail or behind an edge display.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-Front 1
The front face is a dense black panel with the two DB9 COM ports on the bottom row. A blue GPIO connector sits at the left edge of this same panel, while RJ45, USB, HDMI, and DC connectors fill out the rest of the layout.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-Front Angled 2
Let us get into some of these a bit closer, starting with power.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-Power Button 1
The front panel places the power button on the right side adjacent to two indicator lamps. A close-up of the status LEDs reveals two distinct indicators: an amber light marked with a cylinder icon for storage activity, and a green light marked with a bulb icon for system power. These sit just above the main power button on the front bezel.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-LED Indicators 1
The network configuration deserves a closer look because it is not uniform. The system has two Intel I226-IT controllers driving the 2.5GbE ports, plus one Intel I219-LM controller for the single 1GbE port. That third port supports Intel vPro management so while there is no IPMI, you get vPro. We captured all three interfaces in Linux: eno1 and eno2 are the I226-IT parts on PCIe root ports, while eno3 is the I219-LM integrated into the PCH.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-2.5GbE LAN Ports 1
Two white USB Type-A connectors sit above the LAN ports. These are USB 2.0 interfaces, which Supermicro specifies for low-speed peripherals and industrial accessories that do not require higher bandwidth.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-USB 2.0 Type-A Ports 1
The USB 2.0 ports are useful for low-speed peripherals like dongles and serial adapters without wasting the faster USB 3.2 Gen2 ports on the red connectors. For an edge gateway, that is a sensible split because many industrial accessories do not need more than USB 2.0 bandwidth.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-USB 2.0 Type-A Ports 2
Next to the final Ethernet jack, two red Type-A ports are stacked vertically with SuperSpeed USB markings. These provide USB 3.2 Gen2 connectivity for faster external storage or other high-bandwidth devices.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-USB 3.2 Gen2 Type-A Ports 1
Moving across the front panel, two HDMI 2.1 ports provide display output from the integrated Intel Arc B390 GPU. The processor supports up to four displays per Intel’s specifications, and Supermicro exposes two of them on this chassis. Next to those are two male DB9 connectors labeled as COM ports supporting RS-232/422/485.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-HDMI Ports 1
Below the USB and video outputs, a male DB9 connector labeled COM1 is visible. This port supports RS-232/422/485 serial communication, providing legacy industrial interface options alongside modern networking.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-COM Port 1
This close-up shows the second serial connector, labeled COM2. It is a male DB9 port with nine pins and two threaded standoffs for securing cables.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-COM Port 2
The blue female DB9 port on this system is an 8-bit GPIO/SMBus interface.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-GPIO Port 1
The locking DC input sits at the right end of the front panel. Supermicro rates this system for 12V to 36V wide-range DC input, which is a useful feature for industrial sites with existing DC power distribution rather than standard AC outlets. A locking connector is great, since you do not want someone to pull the power out if this is running automation for systems on an assembly line or running an important digital signage kiosk (as examples.)
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-DC Power Input 1
The enclosure itself does most of the thermal work here since there are no fans. The top and bottom surfaces carry pronounced cooling fins that increase surface area for passive heat dissipation. This is a common approach in fanless industrial systems, where the chassis metal becomes the heatsink.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-Top 1
The side panel features three antenna knockouts marked ANT. These openings allow wireless module connectors to pass through when an M.2 radio card is installed.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-Side 2
The rear of the unit is comparatively sparse because most I/O moved to the front. Antenna knockouts on the rear and sides support wireless modules, which can be used with the M.2 E-key slot inside that can host a Wi-Fi or other radio card.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-Rear 1
There are plenty of knockouts for putting antennas around this chassis.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-Rear Angled 1
You can use this box and then have antennas come out of the different sides depending on how you mount it, which we can see being handy in tighter installations.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-Rear Angled 2
The underside has much shallower heatsink fins.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-Bottom 1
Here is the mounting bracket.
Supermicro SYS-E103-14P-H-OTO-30-Accessory 1
With that, let us open the enclosure to examine the mainboard layout and internal components.

The Most Probably Picks for Robert Pattinson's James Bond Cars
45 photos
Photo: Aston Martin
Every new James Bond has been known to inherit a list of at least three things from his predecessor. The first two are the now traditional tuxedo, introduced by Sean Connery’s character in Dr. No, and the Walther PPK (Polizeipistole Kriminal) pistol.
The third is a set of car keys, and each Bond era has left its mark on what cars were driven by the famous British spy. While in Ian Flemming’s novels he originally drove Bentleys, movie 007 has been mostly known to indulge in driving Aston Martins, with the DB5 being by far the most known Bond car.
That said, James Bond has driven anything from the gorgeous Toyota 2000 GT to the Lotus Esprit, and even the BMW Z3, so with each new era we can expect quite a lot of variation in the car brand he is closest to. In November 2026, Amazon MGM studios confirmed that Robert Pattinson will become the seventh actor to portray 007 in the official film series, succeeding Daniel Craig, whose run ended with No Time to Die in 2021.
The first movie with Pattinson as the lead will also be the first one made under Amazon’s creative control, and will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, known for cinematic slam dunks like Arrival, Blade Runner 2049, and the latest Dune films. Steve Knight, known for creating Peaky Blinders, is writing the script, and production is expected to start in the beginning of 2027, with a cinema release likely to happen either by the end of the year or in 2028.
What will the new British spy drive is anyone’s guess for the time being, with this being almost always one of the biggest Bond questions, probably apart from who will play the villain(s). Traditionally, James Bond’s cars have been more than just props, despite some of them adhering to that definition almost 100 percent.
For example, the Aston Martin DB5 in Goldfinger was definitely used initially as a prop, with its ejector seat and onboard Browning machine guns, but it also helped market the shape of a British sports car more than any other model in its day. The Lotus Esprit that turned into a submarine in the Spy Who Loved Me transformed the tiny carmaker from Norfolk into a sports car brand famous around the world.
Each and every Bond car over the years has meant something more than meets the (golden) eye, both for the carmaker that made it and for the James Bond fans. In other words, choosing the next hero car to be driven by 007 is both a commercial but also a culturally significant decision.
Now, at the moment of writing, there is simply no official or unofficial way of knowing more about the next James Bond movie apart from what was said above. With that in mind, I decided to have a go at trying to guess what James Pattinson will get to drive in the next Bond flick. What follows is a list of candidates that I would put in, with some being more obvious than others, but each offering a pretty solid case for joining one of the most famous garages in cinema.
Aston Martin DB5: Because It Wouldn’t Feel Like a Bond Movie Without Its Cameo No matter the actors, story line, direction or script, pretty much every Bond movie needs a scene that tells the audience they are watching a Bond movie. That scene is either the traditional “shaken, not stirred” catchphrase, or a cameo by the most famous Bond car ever, the Aston Martin DB5 .
First introduced in Goldfinger in 1984, where the silver-birch Aston was fitted with machine guns, a bulletproof rear shield, revolving number plates and even an ejector seat and an oil-spilling system, the DB5 has since become almost a permanent fixture in the film series.
Photo: Aston Martin Thanks to its original success, the DB5 has kept returning. After Thunderball in 1965, it came back in GoldenEye and Tomorrow Never Dies in the ‘90s, then in the Daniel Craig era. In Casino Royale, JB wins one in a poker game, while in Skyfall he drives it to Scotland and watches it get destroyed. In Spectre, the DB5 gets rebuilt by Q and in No Time to Die it tears through the streets of Matera, Italy, with its on-board machine guns.
Not including a deleted scene in 1999’s The World Is Not Enough, the Aston Martin DB5 has appeared no less than eight times in Bond films, more than any other car. The reasons for Robert Pattinson driving one are, therefore, many, and the simplest one is that audiences definitely expect it.
Especially when it comes to the introduction of a new Bond, the car doesn’t need to carry the movie, like the original pretty much did in Goldfinger, but it sure does need at least a scene where it reminds everyone in the cinema what movie they are watching. It’s by far the most expected Bond car.
Aston Martin Valen: The Most Hardcore V12-engined Aston For a More Hardcore Bond We don’t yet know how Robert Pattinson’s Bond character will be, but if he’s one that is a bit less of a gentleman than the tuxedoed gentleman of old, it will probably need a car with the same kind of attitude. It’s kind of like the Batmobile driven by Robert was an entirely different animal compared to the old ones.
The Aston Martin Valen is a special-series car developed by Q by Aston Martin, the carmaker’s bespoke division, and it follows the Valour and Valiant as the latest in a line of limited-edition V12 specials. In case it wasn’t obvious by now, Aston’s Q division is a direct nod to Bond’s franchise Q Branch, which also custom-engineers vehicles.
Photo: Aston Martin The Valen’s name apparently comes from the Latin “valens,” meaning strong or powerful, and Aston was definitely not being modest when it named it. With no less than 850 PS (838 HP) and 1,000 Nm (738 lb-ft) of torque, the Aston Martin Valen is the most powerful front-engined production car in the carmaker’s history.
All that power goes strictly to the rear wheels though a transaxle ZF and a limited-slip differential, with Aston quoting just 3.1 seconds required from 0 to 100 kph (62 mph) and an electronically limited top speed of 345 kph (224 mph). I think that would be more than plenty for a high speed chase in the next Bond film.
If Pattinson’s Bond will be a more no-nonsense character than some of its predecessors, the Valen would fit like a glove, not only thanks to its power and performance but also its aggressive design. Sure, it’s a long way from the polished GTs in the Daniel Craig era, but maybe the new Bond won’t spend so much time at cocktail parties.
Aston Martin Valhalla Spider: For When Bond Gets the Girl Or a Coastal Road Scene In almost every Bond movie there has been at least one scene where there is a bit of sunshine, a coastal road and a car with its roof down. In it, 007 is either driving alone with his thoughts, stealing the heart of the next Bond girl or simply running after or from a lower-level villain. That said, Bond is not usually a fan of convertibles, with the last time driving a topless vehicle happening in 2021’s No Time to Die, where 007 is seen driving a two-door, open-top blue Series III Land Rover around Jamaica.
An Aston Martin Valhalla Spider would therefore not be the most obvious choice for a Bond car, despite the coupe version briefly appearing in No Time to Die, albeit without being driven by 007. On top of it, it wasn’t even the production model, but the early AM-RB 003 prototype concept.
Photo: Aston Martin That was a long time ago, and the Aston Martin/007 connection is still as important as ever, and with the world evolving in a more tech-laden area in recent years, maybe it wouldn’t be as far-fetched. The Valhalla Spider is the carmaker’s second-ever series-production mid-engine supercar with a plug-in hybrid system.
In other words, it already has plenty of technology on-board, and everyone knows Bond has always been a fan of gizmos and the latest tech in automotive. The fact that it can be driven topless at car chase speeds is a huge plus as well.
Its powertrain is identical to the coupe, with an AMG-sourced, twin-turbocharged, 4.0-liter flat-plane V8 being paired with three electric motors. Its combined output is a massive 1.079 PS (1,064 HP) and 1,100 Nm (811 lb-ft) of torque, translating into a 0-100 kph (62 mph) time of 2.5 seconds and an electronically limited top speed of 350 kph (217 mph).
Jaguar Type 01: The Electric GT Bond Could Either Drive or Chase Somewhat unsurprisingly, Jaguar has had a long and convoluted history with the James Bond films, usually being driven by the villains, not by 007. In Die Another Day, a villain fights Pierce Brosnan’s Bond on a frozen lake using a gadget-filled Jaguar XKR. In Spectre, Mr. Hinx chases Daniel Craig’s bond through Rome in a C-X75, the hybrid supercar that Jaguar had already cancelled before the movie was made.
Even in No Time to Die, in the famous DB5 scene in Matera, Italy, Bond is being chased by Blofeld’s henchmen driving a Jaguar XF. In other words, the latest Jaguar Type 01 , especially with its windowless rear and bad-guy appearance, could work very well as a Bond villain car.
Photo: Jaguar That said, with the Type 01 representing a new beginning for the Jaguar brand, it wouldn’t be out of the ordinary for the British carmaker to spend some moolah for a different kind of cameo in the next Bond film. For example, M has been constantly driven in Jaguar company cars in the previous films, with one such XJ being used by Bond to escape London in Skyfall.
The Jaguar Type 01 is definitely the most dramatic-looking four-door that Jaguar has made in decades. The electric grand tourer is as long as a full-size sedan but as low as a two-door sports car. Underneath is Jaguar’s new JEA platform, with an 850-volt electrical system and a 118 kWh battery. Its three electric motors develop a combined 1,030 PS (1,015 HP) and 1,365 Nm (1,007 lb-ft) of torque, which is more than enough to propel it away from danger in any Bond car chase.
Still, because of its proportions and size, the Type 01 is not exactly suited for, let’s say, a mountain or back-road chase, since it is more of a grand tourer. A 1,000-horsepower GT that arrives in near silence is a plausible tool for the new M to be driven in, but also quick enough for 007 to get away from any danger, not to mention that it already looks fit to be bullet-proofed.
Lotus Type 135: Also Known As the New Esprit, It Simply Has to Appear in the Movie Apart from the Aston Martin DB5, an upcoming mid-engine supercar from Lotus probably has the biggest chances to become the next Bond’s personal vehicle. Known as the Type 135 during its development, the new model is almost 100 percent expected to get the Esprit name when it goes into production in 2028.
Launched in 1975, the original Esprit had one of the defining shapes of the 1970s and 1980s, with its Giugiaro-designed wedge shape looking like it had arrived from the future. Two years after its launch, Roger Moore as Bond drove a white one off a pier in Sardinia, in the Spy Who Loved Me. Completely unexpected, the white Esprit transformed into a submarine, immediately becoming one of the most famous film cars ever made. “Wet Nellie,” as it was affectionately called by the film crew, now belongs to Elon Musk, who bought it at an auction and has since used it as a canvas for his Tesla chief designer to base the latest Roadster on it.
Photo: Lotus Cars The original Esprit, this time in Turbo guise, also made an appearance as a Bond car in For Your Eyes Only, in 1981, where it sadly destroyed itself when a thief tried to break in. While Lotus ended production in 2004, it has never had a model with the same aura since then.
That may be about to change, as part of the so-called Focus 203 plan, Lotus is currently developing the Type 135, which will be a mid-engine, hybrid V8-powered supercar with more than 1,000 horsepower. Its design was previewed by the Theory 1 concept car, which also harked back to the wedge-look of the original Esprit.
Now, timing is everything, and with the next Bond movie expected to begin in early 2027, the new Esprit’s launch could actually coincide with the date of the cinema launch for the movie. Robert Pattinson’s Bond driving it as the hero car would also close a loop that spans almost half a century, with the original Esprit being the last car that made Lotus famous thanks to good old 007.

Suzuki revives the Ignis as its first global compact EV
The first-generation Ignis went on sale back in 2000 as a three- and five-door hatchback, and in 2016, Suzuki reintroduced it as a compact crossover.
After discontinuing the gas-powered version just last year, Suzuki is now bringing the Ignis back. This time, as a fully electric compact EV.
Suzuki revealed the all-new Ignis EV on Wednesday, deeming it the brand’s “first compact EV for global markets.”
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The electric city car is based on the original Ignis and clearly draws inspiration from the e Sky , Suzuki’s first kei EV that debuted last month in Japan.
Unlike the e Sky, the new Ignis EV is designed for global markets, including Europe. Suzuki said the Ignis was developed under the concept of “Easy to Switch,” which, as you can guess, means it’s designed to make it easy for drivers to switch from a gas-powered car to electric.
Suzuki unveils the all-new Ignis EV (Source: Suzuki)
To ensure it can handle urban areas and winding roads in Europe and other regions, Suzuki put the electric city car through “extensive testing” on public roads.
Suzuki fine-tuned the chassis and power delivery specifically for the different road conditions and needs of drivers in major global markets.
The global Ignis EV is also slightly larger than the e Sky, measuring 3,570 mm long, 1,565 mm wide, and 1,635 mm tall, with a 2,460 mm wheelbase.
The all-new Suzuki Ignis EV (Source: Suzuki)
It’s built on the same dedicated “HEARTECT-e” EV platform as the e Sky, with a single electric motor that delivers 90 hp (67 kW) and 98 lb-ft (133 Nm) of torque.
The Ignis also uses the same 26 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery as the e SKY. However, Suzuki hasn’t revealed driving range figures yet. Suzuki didn’t specify, but the LFP battery pack used in the e SKY is supplied by BYD’s battery unit to keep costs down.
According to Suzuki, the e SKY for Japan offers a WLTC driving range of up to 310 km (192 miles) and a “class-leading” AC energy consumption rating of 97 Wh/km.
The new Suzuki Ignis EV interior (Source: Suzuki)
Inside, the new Suzuki Ignis EV adopts a similar setup to the e Sky with a space-maximizing four-seat layout and a wide infotainment display.
Suzuki will launch the Ignis in Europe and other markets starting in summer 2027. Prices have yet to be announced, but the Ignis will enter an increasingly competitive segment of entry-level compact EVs, including the Renault Twingo, BYD Dolphin Surf, and Honda Super-N.
In Japan, Suzuki’s e SKY undercuts much of the competition with prices starting at just ¥2,120,000 ($13,500).
For context, the Renault Twingo E-Tech starts at under €19,490 ($21,500) in Europe and £14,745 in the UK. BYD’s Dolphin Surf starts at around €22,990 ($25,500) and £18,675 ($24,500) in the UK, while the Honda Super-N starts at £18,995 ($25,000) in the UK.
Which compact EV would you drive? Let us know in the comments. Unfortunately, none of them will be coming to the US.

Ghost Orbital Reentry Vehicle Tailored for 90-Minute Global Delivery Survives Drop Tests
121 photos
Photo: Sierra Space
It's been years already since the Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) announced the start of the Rocket Cargo for Agile Global Logistics program (also known as the Rocket Experimentation for Global Agile Logistics, or REGAL), and to be honest, I almost forgot it existed. Then, Sierra Space got on the line with something to say.
The goal of the REGAL program is to lead to the creation of hardware that can be used for space-based, point-to-point cargo transport. What this means is a spacecraft of sorts that can provide rocket-based space transportation services by launching from a location on the ground, heading high into the atmosphere (and beyond), and then descending upon its target to deliver its payload.
There are several advantages such a system would bring to the table, including the ability to deliver stuff (which can be anything from military equipment to disaster relief supplies) anywhere on the planet in as little as 90 minutes.
Since it was announced, the program has drawn the attention of several private companies, including Sierra Space – the name behind the Dream Chaser spaceplane and the LIFE habitat that will go in the Blue Origin Orbital Reef space station, among other things.
Sierra's proposal for the REGAL program is something called the Ghost. A reentry space vehicle by trade, it meets the AFRL criteria, and now it can even brag about having tested part of its reentry capabilities.
That's because Sierra announced the completion of a drop test campaign that had two versions of the design released from different altitudes to see if they can survive the stresses of reentry and deceleration.
The campaign was conducted at an undisclosed time at the Dugway Proving Ground in Utah, and involved the Ghost XL and Micro Ghost variants of the vehicle. Two drops were performed (it's unclear what other aircraft were involved), from 38,000 feet (11,580 meters) and 67,000 feet (20,400 meters), and they were both successful.
Sierra says these activities validated the reentry capabilities of the Ghost, but it didn't provide any details on what the next steps are in the development of the design.
For what it's worth, the vehicles that were tested are quite far from what the AFRL is looking for with the REGAL effort. The Micro Ghost can carry up to 250 pounds (113 kg), while the XL is rated at up to ten tons. For the record, AFRL wants something that could haul up to 100 tons.
This doesn't mean that Sierra Space is not on the right track, though. The Ghost is intended not as a singular design, but as a family of multi-mission reentry platforms that could be used not only for military needs, but commercial ones as well.

Good News! Gordon Ramsay Leading New BBC Top Gear Lineup From 2028
6 photos
Photo: BBC
Having built a television career by telling people when they've made a mess of things, Gordon Ramsay will host BBC Top Gear from 2028 forward. There is no denying he'll be pointing out some of his culinary hijinks energy at cars as the new lead presenter, and there is no denying the British Broadcasting Corporation has found someone perfectly capable of bringing the show's old magic back.
How much of that old magic will be coming back, that depends just as much on the people standing beside him in front of the cameras. The BBC announced Ramsay as the lead of Top Gear today, with the BBC further confirming that filming begins in 2027. Rather surprisingly, the Dunsfold Aerodrome in Surrey is returning as Top Gear's home base. What a time to be alive, huh?
The Stig is also back, presumably still unwilling to explain if he's a Mariah Carey-loving cyborg who loves gardening in his free time. Beyond Gordon and the anonymous tame racing driver created by Wilman and Clarkson a long time ago, the identities of Ramsay's co-presenters have yet to be announced.
In any case, there is more to this appointment than putting a famous chef behind the steering wheel of the latest Ferrari . Born in 1966, the new host is a genuine car lover whose automotive interest predates the television career and restaurant empire. Ramsay grew up near Silverstone, where he would climb over fences to catch a glimpse of the racing.
Ayrton Senna became his Formula 1 hero, and his passion for motorsports has remained part of this life rather than something acquired for a television appearance. The bloke is one of us, for real. His garage also suggests that Gordon has more experience with interesting machinery than the average celebrity, with Ramsay owning an extensive collection of exotics.
Photo: Gordon Ramsay on Facebook Over the years, Ramsay appeared on Top Gear on three occasions. It all started in 2002, then returned in 2006 and 2017, respectively. During his second appearance, Ramsay set a 1:45 lap in the reasonably priced Chevrolet Lacetti, putting him seventh on the leaderboard. Gordon also holds a racing license and has participated in track driving.
The BBC has, therefore, hired someone who understands the appeal of cars, enjoys the act of driving them, and knows how television works. There is, however, a problem with the BBC's announcement. That problem has haunted the British Broadcasting Corporation since Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond, and James May left the BBC in 2015.
I can't believe it's been more than a decade, and I certainly can't believe that the three amigos have also wrapped up The Grand Tour in September 2024. Instead of retiring the brand after the original trio's partnership ended, Amazon handed the keys to a digitally native lineup comprising Thomas Holland and James Engelsman of Throttle House, plus social media personality Francis Bourgeois.
JC, Hammond, and Captain Slow had spent years developing a relationship that proved much harder to reproduce than the BBC seemed to appreciate. Clarkson was the ringleader, Hamster the enthusiastic foil, and May the oft-exasperated voice of reason. Their arguments, distinct approaches to cars, and shared history made even a relatively ordinary episode feel special.
All of the BBC's attempts to replace them failed, demonstrating how much audiences had associated the show with its former hosts. Ramsay's appointment gives the BBC a plausible way back, but as everyone may have already guessed, Top Gear is not a one-man show. For the BBC, finding Gordon 's Hamster and Captain Slow is the job that will decide whether Top Gear has genuinely returned.
